segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: I’ve brought my notes on our Biology Field Trip to Rocky Bay, Colin, so we can work on our report on the research we did together.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: OK. I’ve got mine too. Let’s look at the aims of the trip first.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Right. What did you have?

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: I just put something about getting experience of the different sorts of procedures used on a field trip. But we need something about what causes different organisms to choose particular habitats.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: I agree. And something about finding out how to protect organisms in danger of dying out?

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: In our aims? But we weren’t really looking at that.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: I suppose not. OK, now there’s the list of equipment we all had to bring on the field trip. What did they tell us to bring a ruler for?

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: It was something about measuring the slope of the shore, but of course we didn’t need it because we were measuring wind direction, and we’d brought the compass for that ...

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: But not the piece of string to hold up in the air! Didn’t Mr Blake make a fuss about us leaving that behind.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Yeah. He does go on. Anyway it was easy to get one from another of the students.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Now, the next section’s the procedure. I sent you the draft of that.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Yeah. It was clear, but I don’t think we need all these details of what time we left and what time we got back and how we divided up the different research tasks.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: OK. I’ll look at that again.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Then we have to describe our method of investigation in detail. So let’s begin with how we measured wave speed. I was surprised how straightforward that was.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: I’d expected us to have some sort of high-tech device, not just stand there and count the number of waves per minute. Not very precise, but I suppose it was good enough. But the way we measured the amount of salt was interesting.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: In the water from the rock pools?

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Yeah, oh, I wanted to check the chemicals we used in the lab when we analysed those samples – was it potassium chromate and silver nitrate?

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: That’s right.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: OK. And we need the map of the seashore. You just left that to me. And I had to do in while the tide was low, well that was OK, but the place I started it from was down on the beach, then I realised I should have gone up higher to get better visibility, so I had to start all over again. But at least I’d go the squared paper or I’d have had problems drawing it all to scale.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Yes. It looks good. We could get a map of the region off the internet and see if we need to make any changes.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: I had a look but I couldn’t find anything. But you took some pictures, didn’t you?

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Yeah. I’ll email you them if you want.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: OK. I’ll make my amendments using those, then I can scan it into our report. Great.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Now when we get to our findings I thought we could divide them up into the different zones we identified on the shore and the problems organisms face in each zone. So for the highest area ...

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: ... the splash zone?

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Yeah, we found mostly those tiny shellfish that have strong hard shells that act as protection.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: But not from other organisms that might eat them, predators?

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: No, that’s not the main danger for them. But the shells prevent them from drying out because they’re in the open air for most of the time. ( & )

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Right. And since they’ve exposed, they need to be able to find some sort of shelter, or cover themselves up, so they don’t get too hot ( & ). Then in the middle and lower zones, nearer the sea, we need to discuss the effects of wave action ...

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Yes, and how organisms develop structures to prevent themselves from being swept away, or even destroyed by being smashed against the rocks.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: I haven’t done anything on the geological changes. I don’t know what to put for that.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: No, we weren’t concentrating on that. Maybe we need to find some websites.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Good idea. I’ve got the lecture notes from Mr Blake’s geology course, but they’re too general. But we could ask him which books on our Reading List might be most helpful.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Right. OK, now I did a draft of the section of sources of possible error in our research, but I don’t know if you agree. For example, the size of the sample, and whether it’s big enough to make any general conclusions from. But I thought actually we did have quite a big sample.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: We did. And our general method of observation seemed quite reliable. But we might not be all that accurate as far as the actual numbers go.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Yeah, we might have missed some organisms – if they were hiding under a rock, for example ( & ). I wasn’t sure about the way we described their habitats. I decided it was probably OK.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Yeah, and the descriptions we gave of the smaller organisms, they weren’t very detailed, but they were adequate in this context. I’m not sure we identified all the species correctly thought. ( & )

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: OK, we’d better mention that. Now, how ...

questions.source_text:
SECTION 3
Questions 21-30
ROCKY BAY FIELD TRIP
Choose the correct letter A, B or C.
Questions:
    Q Num: 21
    Text: What do the students agree should be included in their aims?
    Options:
        factors affecting where organisms live.
        the need to preserve endangered species.
        techniques for classifying different organisms.
    Q Num: 22
    Text: What equipment did they forget to take on the Field Trip?
    Options:
        string.
        a compass.
        a ruler.
    Q Num: 23
    Text: In Helen's procedure section, Colin suggests a change in
    Options:
        the order in which information is given.
        the way the information is divided up.
        the amount of information provided.
    Q Num: 24
    Text: What do they say about the method they used to measure wave speed?
    Options:
        It provided accurate results.
        It was simple to carry out.
        It required special equipment.
    Q Num: 25
    Text: What mistake did Helen make when first drawing the map?
    Options:
        She chose the wrong scale.
        She stood in the wrong place.
        She did it at the wrong time.
    Q Num: 26
    Text: What do they decide to do next with their map?
    Options:
        scan it onto a computer.
        check it using photographs.
        add information from the internet.
Choose TWO letters A–E.
Q Num: 27
Text: Which TWO problems affecting organisms in the splash zone are mentioned?
Count: 2
Options:
    Id: A
    Text: lack of water
    Id: B
    Text: strong winds
    Id: C
    Text: lack of food
    Id: D
    Text: high temperatures
    Id: E
    Text: large waves
Choose TWO letters A–E.
Q Num: 29
Text: Which TWO reasons for possible error will they include in their report?
Count: 2
Options:
    Id: A
    Text: inaccurate records of the habitat of organisms
    Id: B
    Text: influence on behaviour of organisms by observer
    Id: C
    Text: incorrect identification of some organisms
    Id: D
    Text: making generalisations from a small sample
    Id: E
    Text: missing some organisms when counting
